content:
Understanding the role of motivation in engaging students in laboratory skill education is paramount for enhancing learning outcomes and academic achievement. Traditional physical laboratories in science education serve as experiential learning environments, facilitating the development of high-level conceptual understanding among students. The attitudes students hold towards these laboratories can significantly influence the effectiveness of skill training. In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, computer-based virtual laboratories (VLs) emerged as viable alternatives for skill training and experimentation, particularly under lockdown restrictions. Nevertheless, there exists a considerable gap in the adoption of VLs, largely attributed to the lack of awareness and familiarity among educators and students.

This study sought to investigate the key motivational factors that impact the efficacy of VLs in imparting laboratory skills and tasks. Data for this study was gathered through several instruments: the Intrinsic Motivation Inventory (IMI) scale, self-reported survey responses focusing on extrinsic factors, and a teachers' VL perception scale. Analytical methods included independent sample t-tests and automatic linear modeling (LINEAR) to rigorously assess the data.

The findings of this research indicate that animated graphic learning materials in VLs exert a more substantial influence on students' intrinsic motivation compared to e-book learning materials. Furthermore, the involvement of teachers plays a critical role in elevating students' motivational levels when engaging in laboratory experiments via VLs. Additionally, the study reveals that prolonged engagement or repeated exposure to VL experiments positively affects students' laboratory performance.

Overall, the study underscores the importance of integrating motivating elements within virtual laboratory environments to enhance student engagement and skill acquisition, while highlighting the pivotal role educators play in facilitating this process.
